title: llm-brain default
description: General taste and PR-hygiene rules for any repo. Company profiles extend this one.

P01.title: Title format
P01.what: The PR title is a conventional commit: `type(scope): summary`, with an allowed type (and scope, if the profile lists scopes).
P01.remedy: Use a conventional title: `type(scope): what changes`.

P02.title: Issue reference
P02.what: The tracking issue `#N` appears in the branch, every commit subject and the PR title, and it is the same issue everywhere.
P02.remedy: Put the tracking issue `#N` in the branch, every commit subject and the PR title.

P03.title: How to verify
P03.what: The description has a How to verify / Testing section with real steps (skipped for tiny PRs).
P03.remedy: Add a `How to verify` section: numbered steps a teammate can follow, and what they should see.

P10.title: Long title
P10.what: The title is at most 72 characters.
P10.remedy: Cut the title to one change in at most 72 characters; details go in the body.

P12.title: Long description
P12.what: The description fits a word budget that grows a little with the size of the change (200 words plus 0.2 per added line, at most 450).
P12.remedy: Cut the description to the budget: why (1-2 sentences), what changes for users, risks, how to verify. Leave out what the diff already shows.

P13.title: Description restates the code
P13.what: The description is not mostly inline code: at most 6 code spans per 100 words.
P13.remedy: Describe behaviour and intent in words. Drop identifier lists, class strings and file moves the diff already shows.

P14.title: Private references
P14.what: The description does not lean on references a teammate can't resolve, like `§5.4`, `AC2`, `slice 3` or `Vitalii's 194` (a review-comment number).
P14.remedy: Spell out what `§5.4`-style or `AC2`-style references mean, or link the document. A teammate must not need your notes.

P15.title: Session narration
P15.what: The description does not narrate the author's session or tools ("in this session", "the browser extension was not connected", "I have implemented").
P15.remedy: Remove notes about the author's tools or session. If something was not tested, say what and why in one line under How to verify.

P16.title: Promotional wording
P16.what: The description does not use two or more promotional words (comprehensive, robust, seamless, leverage...).
P16.remedy: Replace adjectives with facts: what changed, measured how.

P17.title: Placeholder text
P17.remedy: Fill in or delete the template placeholders.

P18.title: Missing description
P18.what: A non-trivial PR has a description of at least 15 words.
P18.remedy: Write two sentences: what changes and why. Then how to verify.

P19.title: Which issue?
P19.what: The PR closes one issue, and it is the one its title names.
P19.remedy: Close exactly one issue, and make it the one the title names. Mention related issues as "Related: #N".

C01.title: Temporary commits
C01.what: No `fixup!`, `squash!` or `wip` commits left in the branch.
C01.remedy: Squash `fixup!`/`wip` commits or give them real subjects.

C02.title: Committed secret
C02.what: No credentials (private keys, cloud/API tokens) in the diff, the PR text or commit messages. Blocks on its own.
C02.remedy: Revoke the credential now, remove it from the branch history, and load it from the secret store.

C04.title: Vague commit subjects
C04.what: Commit subjects say what changed; no bare `fix`, `update`, `wip`.
C04.remedy: Say what each commit changes; `fix`, `update`, `wip` alone tell a reader nothing.

Z01.title: Too big to review
Z01.what: At most 800 changed lines (added lines, plus half the deleted ones), not counting generated files, lockfiles and fixtures.
Z01.remedy: Split it: land the refactor, then the behaviour change, then the follow-ups. Each PR should be reviewable in one sitting.

Z02.title: Several changes in one title
Z02.what: The title names at most two changes.
Z02.remedy: One PR, one change. Split independent items into their own PRs.

K01.title: Debug output
K01.remedy: Remove debug output, or log through the project logger at a deliberate level.

K02.title: Suppression without a reason
K02.what: Every lint/type suppression (`@ts-ignore`, `eslint-disable`, `nolint`, `noqa`, `#[allow]`...) carries a reason.
K02.remedy: Fix the warning, or keep the narrowest suppression with the reason next to it.

K03.title: TypeScript any
K03.remedy: Use the real type, a generic, or `unknown` and narrow it.

K04.title: Rust unwrap
K04.what: No new `.unwrap()` in Rust library/server code (tests, examples and binaries excluded).
K04.remedy: Return the error with `?` or handle it; a panic in a request path takes the worker down.

K05.title: Swallowed Go error
K05.what: No swallowed Go errors: empty `if err != nil {}` or `_ =` on calls that return errors.
K05.remedy: Handle or return the error. If ignoring it is right, say why in a comment.

K06.title: Shell failure ignored
K06.what: Shell scripts don't hide failures with `|| true`.
K06.remedy: Handle the failure you expect (`[[ -e f ]] && rm f`) instead of hiding every failure.

K07.title: Python bare except
K07.what: No bare `except:` / `except Exception: pass` in Python.
K07.remedy: Catch the exception you expect and handle it, or let it propagate.

K08.title: SQL built from strings
K08.what: SQL is never built by string formatting or concatenation.
K08.remedy: Bind values as parameters. Pick column/table names from a fixed map.

K09.title: Unfinished code
K09.what: No unfinished code: `todo!()`, `unimplemented!()`, `panic("TODO")`, `throw new Error("not implemented")`.
K09.remedy: Finish it or take the unfinished path out of this PR.

D01.title: TODO without a ticket
D01.remedy: Link the follow-up issue in the TODO (`TODO(#123): ...`) or do it now.

D05.title: Commented-out code
D05.remedy: Delete it; git keeps the history.

D02.title: Comments that narrate the code
D02.what: Comments say why, not what. A comment that only repeats the next line of code counts against the PR. (Judged by Jev.)

params.question: Does this added comment only restate what the code right after it plainly does?
params.yes: Deleting the comment loses nothing: no reason, constraint, contract, warning or domain fact; it paraphrases the next lines (e.g. '// loop over users' above a for loop, '// return the result' above return).
params.no: It explains why, a non-obvious constraint, a contract, a gotcha or domain knowledge, or it is a required doc comment on a public API.
params.finding: this comment repeats the code below it

D02.remedy: Delete comments that repeat the code. Keep the ones that say why.

D03.title: Docs contradict the code
D03.what: The description and comments don't claim something the code contradicts. (Judged by Jev.)

params.question: Does the PR description or a changed comment claim something the shown code contradicts?
params.yes: A specific statement (e.g. 'newest shown', 'retries 3 times') conflicts with a visible line of code in the diff.
params.no: Statements match the code, or a contradiction cannot be established from what is shown.
params.finding: the description or a comment says something the code contradicts

D03.remedy: Make the description and comments say what the code does, or fix the code.

T01.title: No test changes
T01.what: A change of 100+ production lines (or a new 30+ line file) changes or adds tests.
T01.remedy: Add tests for the risky path, or say in the PR which existing tests cover it.

T02.title: Tests that assert nothing
T02.remedy: Assert on a real result that would fail if the behaviour broke.

T03.title: Skipped tests
T03.what: Skipped tests carry a reason and an issue.
T03.remedy: Fix the test, or skip it with a reason and the issue that will re-enable it.

T04.title: Untested behaviour change
T04.what: The risky behaviour change has a test or a verification step that would catch a regression. (Judged by Jev.)

params.question: Does this PR change behaviour in a way that has a concrete regression scenario which neither the changed tests nor the verification steps exercise?
params.yes: You can name an input or event, the expected result and the changed code path, and no shown test or verification step checks it.
params.no: The shown tests or steps cover the risky path, the change does not alter behaviour, or there is not enough evidence.
params.finding: a behaviour change has a regression case no test or verify step covers

T04.remedy: Add a test for the scenario named in the review, with the failing input and the expected result.

S01.title: Copy-pasted blocks
S01.what: No copy-pasted blocks of 10+ lines inside the change.
S01.remedy: Reuse one implementation, or say why the copies must change independently.

S02.title: Unused new helper
S02.what: No new private helpers that nothing calls.

S03.title: Abstraction nobody needs
S03.what: No layers, wrappers or options that no caller needs. (Judged by Jev.)

params.question: Does this added code introduce a layer, wrapper, option or generic abstraction that no shown caller needs, making the code harder to follow than a direct version?
params.yes: A simpler direct version would keep the same behaviour; the abstraction has one caller and no stated second use (e.g. a factory for one type, a config flag nothing sets, a wrapper that only forwards).
params.no: The abstraction has several real uses, is required by a framework or interface, or there is not enough context to tell.
params.finding: a layer or option no caller needs

S03.remedy: Inline the layer. Add the abstraction when the second real use arrives.

S04.title: Error turned into success
S04.what: Failures are not quietly turned into success. (Judged by Jev.)

params.question: Does this added code turn a real failure into apparent success (swallow, log-and-continue, or return a default) without a stated reason?
params.yes: A failing operation can be named whose error is dropped or replaced by a success value, and nothing says this is intended.
params.no: The error propagates, recovery is deliberate and explained, or the hunk has no error path.
params.finding: a failure is turned into apparent success

S04.remedy: Propagate the failure, or handle it on purpose and say why in a comment.

S05.title: Should be split
S05.what: One PR, one change: independently shippable parts are separate PRs. (Judged by Jev.)

params.question: Does this PR bundle two or more changes that could ship, be reviewed and be reverted independently?
params.yes: At least two parts serve different outcomes and either could land alone (e.g. a new column plus an unrelated keyboard change plus an investigation write-up).
params.no: The parts are one coherent change, or one is a required prerequisite of the other.
params.finding: independent changes are bundled into one PR

S05.remedy: Split the independent parts into their own PRs.

J01.title: Unclear what and why
J01.what: From the title and the first two sentences, a teammate can say what changes and why. (Judged by Jev.)

params.question: Would a teammate who has not seen this work be unable to say what changes and why, from only the title and the first two sentences of the description?
params.yes: The opening is jargon, a list of items, internal references, or file/class names, and does not say what changes for users or the system and why.
params.no: The title and opening plainly state the change and its reason.
params.finding: the title and first two sentences don't say what changes and why

J01.remedy: Open with one plain sentence: what changes for users or the system, and why.

J02.title: Description reads like a work log
J02.what: The description is for the reviewer, not a work log: no restating the diff, session notes, other issues' investigations or other PRs. (Judged by Jev.)

params.question: Does the description spend much of its length on things a reviewer does not need: restating the diff, the author's tooling or session, investigations for other issues, or work from other PRs?
params.yes: Large parts list identifiers or class strings, narrate the process, diagnose a different issue, or describe other PRs.
params.no: Nearly everything helps a reviewer understand intent, risk, or how to verify.
params.finding: much of the description is a work log (restated diff, session notes, other issues)

J02.remedy: Keep only what a reviewer needs: why, what changes for users, risk, how to verify. Move investigations to their issue.

J03.title: Behaviour change buried
J03.what: Every behaviour change users or API clients will notice is stated plainly near the top. (Judged by Jev.)

params.question: Does this PR change user-visible or API behaviour that the description does not state plainly near the top?
params.yes: A behaviour change (e.g. single click now selects instead of opens; a field renamed) is missing or buried in a parenthesis deep in the body.
params.no: Every behaviour change is stated plainly near the top, or there is none.
params.finding: a behaviour change users will notice is missing or buried

J03.remedy: List every behaviour change users or API clients will notice, near the top.
